text:
anya: heads-up — experimenting with a lightweight sidecar shim for model selection. idea: let gateway set X-Model-Prefer and sidecar map to alias+version pins. thoughts?
mike: curious. how is this better than header-only rules in gateway?
anya: 2 reasons: 1) can do tenant-local overrides without changing global routing rules. 2) sidecar can query local compat matrix before pinning.
ravi: concern: quotas. if sidecar rewrites to a newer version we need to charge the right quota. gateway needs to see final model id.
mike: agreed. sidecar should set X-Resolved-Model after negotiation, gateway uses that for billing/telemetry.
sre-ops: failure modes? if sidecar dies we need fallback to gateway-level default alias. also healthcheck semantics.
liz: console UX note: rollout panels must show both requested header and resolved model, plus compat reason. otherwise SRE will be confused.
anya: provisional routing snippet:
```yaml
route:
  match: tenant == "acme" && header("x-ml-intent") == "summarize"
  action: set_header("x-model-prefer", "gptx-small:alias=stable")
```
then sidecar does negotiation -> sets `X-Resolved-Model: gptx-small:v1.4-q8`.
ravi: also need a telemetry tag for 'negotiation_path' (e.g., alias->compat_filter->quant-profile).
mike: +1. store negotiation_path as string list in traces. helps eval regressions.
liz: about pinning semantics: if tenant requests strict pin via header 'x-model-pin: exact', sidecar must respect and return error if incompatible.
anya: proposal: precedence order: explicit pin header > route policy alias > tenant default alias. Sidecar may downgrade only within compat range unless 'exact' set.
sre-ops: and quota accounting: gateway uses X-Resolved-Model for metering, but we should also emit X-Requested-Model for audit.
console-bot: deploy note: sidecar v0.3 rolled to staging. telemetry: https://telemetry/reports/2345 :eyes:
mike: next steps: I'll mock a sidecar prototype that emits resolved headers + trace. will ping for quick review.
anya: thanks. can someone add a short note in the routing UX backlog? @liz
liz: on it, created task RF-812, linked in the thread.
